_comment: When it is safe to cross the high and icy ground, by time of day.
ASSUME IT SNOWS. Do not plan around whether a storm arrives — plan around
being BEHIND THE PLOWS AND IN DAYLIGHT. State crews work 12-hour shifts
around the clock during a storm and stage before it starts, with the aim of
having priority routes clear for the morning commute. So the road you want
is the same road four hours later, and the mistake is leaving at 4am to get
a jump on the day.
SCHEMA
plowedBy  local clock time this is NORMALLY clear behind the plows. Earlier
than this you are the plow's problem. THE FIELD THAT MATTERS.
priority  where this sits in the state's plowing order
daylight  true when the crossing should also be inside daylight, which the
app computes for the real date rather than storing it here
plows     who runs them and how hard
risk      what actually goes wrong
car       what it means for a FWD Accord on all-season touring tires
watch     the state's own road conditions source
tz        hours from UTC in STANDARD time. Arizona keeps no DST and Monteagle
is Central, not Eastern — neither is guessable from longitude.
`plowedBy` is typical, not promised. In an active storm the road is being
cleared continuously and the honest answer is that it is never finished —
the time is when the last pass is normally far enough ahead of you.

points.name: Tehachapi Pass
points.plows: Caltrans plows CA-58 through the night. It is the road that usually stays open when I-5 over the Grapevine closes, which is why the route uses it.
points.risk: Chain control rather than closure. R1 and R2 go up during a storm and come down within hours of it ending.
points.car: Under R2 a FWD car needs chains ON — the exemption is 4WD only and does not apply to you. This is the first climb of the whole trip, a couple of hours from home.

points.name: Flagstaff
points.plows: ADOT stages plows on I-40 before the storm arrives and runs them around the clock. Interstates are cleared first; state routes wait until the interstates are done.
points.risk: The highest ground on the western half and the most likely place to find the interstate shut outright. Reopenings usually come mid-morning.
points.car: Fine behind the plows. The danger is being on it at 5am, or during the storm itself.

points.name: Grand Canyon Village
points.plows: Park crews, not ADOT. The rim road and the south entrance are plowed and stay open all winter, but they start after the state has done the interstate.
points.risk: The entrance road can close during a storm. Snow on the rim makes the canyon better, not worse.
points.car: No problem once cleared. Give it an extra hour over the interstate.

points.name: Desert View
points.plows: National Park Service, and this is not a priority road. Desert View Drive is closed for winter storms while the south entrance stays open.
points.risk: The highest point on the whole trip and the first thing to shut. It may not reopen the same day at all.
points.car: The canyon road is a fair-weather choice. If it has snowed overnight, take the plain interstate through Williams and do the canyon another time.

points.name: Continental Divide
points.plows: NMDOT treats I-40 as a first-priority route and plows it continuously through a storm.
points.risk: Exposed high ground. Blowing snow closes it more often than snowfall does, and drifting can undo a plowed road within the hour.
points.car: Crosswind on ice is the hazard here, not depth. Wind does not care that the plow has been through, so this one wants daylight most of all.

points.name: Amarillo
points.plows: TxDOT pre-treats with brine for days ahead of a forecast storm and then asks drivers to stay off the road. The Panhandle does not carry the plow fleet the mountain states do, because it does not usually need one.
points.risk: ICE, not snow, and brine works before the ice rather than after it. There is no plow pass that fixes a glazed road, so `plowedBy` here really means 'once the sun has been on it'.
points.car: Nothing you can carry fixes ice. If the Panhandle is glazed, the plan is to stop early and lose the afternoon, not to drive it slowly.

points.name: Childress
points.plows: The same TxDOT operation as Amarillo with fewer crews. US-287 sits below I-40 in the order, so it is treated later.
points.risk: Panhandle ice with less attention paid to it. This is the leg 3 road, so it is an early-January problem on the way home.
points.car: Treat exactly like Amarillo, and expect it to be worse for longer.

points.name: Oklahoma City
points.plows: ODOT does carry plows and clears interstates and highways first, but Oklahoma's winter is freezing rain more than snowfall.
points.risk: Bridges and overpasses glaze first and stay bad long after the open pavement is fine. A cleared road here is not a cleared bridge.
points.car: The overpasses are the hazard. Slow before them, not on them.

points.name: Monteagle
points.plows: TDOT pre-treats and plows the I-24 grade, but maintenance is not really the issue here.
points.risk: The climb is the worst ice trap between Nashville and Atlanta. Trucks jackknife on the grade and shut the road behind them, which costs far more time than the ice would.
points.car: Your risk is other people's trucks. If it is iced, wait at the bottom rather than joining the queue on the hill.

points.name: Asheville
points.plows: NCDOT plows I-40, but the mountain section through the gorge is steep, curved and shaded, so it holds ice for hours after the flat roads have cleared.
points.risk: I-40 climbs through the Smokies to reach here and does ice up. The Blue Ridge Parkway closes outright and stays closed all winter.
points.car: Shade is why this one is late. The southern line through Atlanta exists for exactly this day.

points.name: Atlanta
points.plows: GDOT keeps limited winter equipment for a city this size, because it needs it about twice a decade.
points.risk: Atlanta ices rarely and completely. When it does the city stops, the interstates fill with abandoned cars, and no plowing schedule applies.
points.car: If a named winter storm is heading for Atlanta, be somewhere else. This is the one place on the trip where the answer is not a time of day.
